Sometimes WOLF pointedly looks away. He is noticing things for himself, not acting as a pickup detector.
realism_features.how: Write an authored, deterministic rule in main.gd: if WOLF is within about 120 px and the item's catalog entry has a wolf_reaction (notice / avert / none), set WOLF's flip_h toward the item and tween wolf.body_sprite rotation by a small amount, then snap back to WOLF_SPRITE_REST. Play servo at a pitch set by the reaction. This is never triggered by proximity alone before the player shows interest (in reach for more than 1 s), so WOLF does not become a metal detector. There is no runtime AI and no meter.

inventory.what_you_collect: Optional evidence that the engineer finds or copies while moving through the rooms: logs read off wall screens, physical photographs and prints, data fragments pulled from secondary consoles, and small personal or technical objects that have examine text. The two essential-path records (the purge-order trace and the mirror trace) also appear in the locker. They are derived from the existing purge_trace_preserved and mirror_trace_preserved flags and are never stored twice. There are no weapons, no consumables, no slot limit and no scarcity.
item_kinds: LOG: text copied from a diegetic wall screen by holding USE (it has a copy progress bar)
PHOTO: a found physical print or ID image shown as a thumbnail in the journal
DATA: a fragment pulled from a console. The two essential traces are derived DATA entries.
OBJECT: a physical artefact with examine text. Several can grow a later WOLF annotation.
example_items_per_room: Maintenance corridor: [LOG-A] a maintenance log on a wall screen in the free floor between the breaker and the relay (about x 440-520, clear of the 350 and 605 station reach)
Maintenance corridor: [OBJECT-A] a dropped personal item before the seal (about x 690-740, clear of the safe point at 876)
Maintenance corridor: [PHOTO-A] a pinned print near the purge display, placed at about x 260-290 so it stays outside the x<=230 USE claim
Records Access: [DATA-PURGE] and [DATA-MIRROR], derived automatically from the existing trace flags
Records Access: [DATA-A] a fragment on a secondary console (about x 300-420), the safest first pickup because this room has no hazards
Records Access: [PHOTO-B] an ID image or print between the mirror port and the exit (about x 620-760)
Service Junction: [OBJECT-B] a tag or tool at the entry (about x 40-140, before the breaker at 200)
Service Junction: [LOG-B] a screen readout in the sentry lane (about x 760-790) that spawns only once the sentry is down, so it never lures the player into a knockdown
Example names only: Nathanial writes every real name, examine line and WOLF annotation
inventory.how_items_are_used: Items are read and examined, never spent. Opening an entry shows its examine text. If the engineer examined it with WOLF nearby, or a related item was also found, the entry gains a WOLF annotation or a 'corroborates [OTHER]' line. That line is computed from the set of collected items, not stored (an Outer Wilds-lite web that grows like Hollow Knight's Hunter's Journal). Nothing unlocks a route, a door or an ending in this slice. A later chapter may react to what was collected, but only through authored, optional dialogue that Nathanial decides on. The project's no-morality-meter rule holds: no score, percentage or rating.
inventory.ui: Add a LOCKER button in Pause between Resume and Settings, and reflow the panel to Resume 133 / Locker 192 / Settings 251 / Title 310 with 52 px buttons and a panel about 450 px tall. A new InventoryMenu Control sits as a sibling of SettingsMenu and reuses the expanded 760x464 panel. The left column lists entries grouped by room. Each row is at least 52 px tall and shows a text kind tag (LOG / PHOTO / DATA / OBJECT, never colour alone) and an unread dot for collected-but-unexamined items. The right pane holds a code-drawn icon or thumbnail, the name, the examine text in a RichTextLabel (escaped as the changelog is, with held-direction and drag scrolling reused), a 'WOLF:' annotation block once earned and a 'Found in: [room]' line. Undiscovered entries are not listed, so there are no completion counts or empty-slot silhouettes. In-world feedback is the status line 'Logged to locker: [NAME]' and a small unread pip on the existing Pause control (touch top-right). There is no new HUD button. Focus is set explicitly: grab_focus on the first row, focus_neighbor_* set in code, and back/cancel routed through PauseOverlay._input (which emits back_requested when either submenu is visible), main._handle_back() and _menu_focus_target().
inventory.wolf_role: WOLF is an independent witness, not a pack mule or an item radar. He reacts to some finds on his own terms (turns toward them, avoids looking at them, or says nothing) and adds his own annotation to certain entries. Annotations are authored, deterministic and conditioned on real state such as the earlier relay choice memory or the mirror route taken. He can disagree with what an item seems to mean. He never fetches, carries or uses items, so collecting stays the engineer's act.
inventory.engineer_fallback: Every item can be reached and collected by the engineer alone through tap or hold USE inside its own reach. None needs WOLF or a choice button. WOLF annotations are extra layers on entries the engineer already holds. Because nothing is essential, the game can be finished with an empty locker, and a scene test proves this. The essential traces keep their existing engineer-only routes (the manual mirror route) and only appear in the locker because those flags are set.
inventory.save_model: Raise SAVE_VERSION to 5. to_dict adds "evidence": {"collected": [...], "examined": [...], "annotated": [...]}, with each array a sorted list of String ids so the save bytes stay deterministic. from_dict gets a fifth layer, `if data["version"] >= 5:`, after the v4 block. Its checks: evidence is a Dictionary; all three are Arrays of Strings with no duplicates and sorted; every id is in the catalog with approved=true; derived ids (the trace entries) are rejected if stored; annotated is a subset of examined, which is a subset of collected; each item's chapter is at or before the saved chapter_id in CHAPTER_IDS order; and each item's requires flag is true in the same save (e.g. the lane log needs sentry_down). Saves below v5 load with an empty locker, and no optional item is granted retroactively. On pickup or examine, update state, patch only the evidence section of beat_snapshot (keeping its positions), and call _write_beat() only when state.checkpoint_reached. Never call _save_progress(), because it recaptures position and would make the sentry lane the restore point. Examines made while paused are written on resume. Unread is derived as collected minus examined. A knockdown restore therefore keeps items, and a corridor run before the safe point keeps them in the snapshot until the first save.

options.input_mapping: No new gameplay action or on-screen button. Take, read and copy all use the existing interact action, so remapping applies automatically: tap USE to take an object or photo or to read a screen line, and hold USE (hold_use.gd) to copy a log, with release cancelling. Pickups are disabled while waiting_for_choice so they never compete with WOLF's two choice buttons. Keyboard: E/Space (or the remapped key) to take, read or copy; Esc/P to Pause, then Locker. In the Locker, Up/Down or W/S move through entries, Enter opens the detail pane, held Up/Down scrolls long text and Esc goes back to Pause. Controller: A takes, reads or copies; Start pauses; D-pad or left stick navigates; A selects; B goes back; held D-pad or the right stick scrolls detail text. Touch: the existing USE button relabels to TAKE, READ or COPY (hold) in reach, and the existing top-right Pause control (with an unread pip) leads to the Locker. Tap a row to open it, drag the detail text to scroll (emulated mouse events are ignored as in the changelog) and use the in-panel BACK button to return.
options.art_needed: First pass is entirely code-drawn with no new provenance: pickup props as Node2D _draw recipes (tablet, print, tag, data chip, tool), the dust-outline collected state, glints from RoomDepth.make_glow, WallScreen bezels and faces, scanline bands, and journal icons per kind. Environmental dressing is also code-drawn (scorch decals, a dropped bag, a jammed locker, a smear). Optional second pass: Codex image_gen paintings for PHOTO thumbnails and a few hero props. Each needs Nathanial's approval and an asset-register entry (prompt, date, tool, approval) in apps/game/assets/manifest.json. That entry is blocked until the in-progress merge conflict in manifest.json (the <<<<<<< HEAD markers around line 216) is resolved on main. Catalog entries with approved=false never spawn and never ship text or art.
options.audio_needed: All procedural in SfxBank: seeded, deterministic, peak-checked and inside the generation_ms budget. Footsteps (3 surfaces x 2 actors x 3-4 variants), 4-6 room tone chunks per room, one-shot sets (distant hull bang, cooling tick, drip, vent flutter, far servo), pickup handling sounds (paper rustle, plastic clack, tag clink, data chirp), screen sounds (copy-progress ticks, a completion chirp, a CRT whine under the bed) and journal UI sounds (open, page, close) on the Effects bus. A runtime Room bus sends to Effects and carries a per-room AudioEffectReverb. No recorded audio is needed. If a CC0 sample is ever substituted, it is logged with its source URL and licence in the asset register.
risks: The worktree is mid-merge: manifest.json, README.md and several docs files are in the UU state and manifest.json is not valid JSON. Provenance entries and the 'merge everything into main' request both depend on resolving this first.

Story text gate: all item names, examine lines, screen wording and WOLF annotations need Nathanial's approval. Until then approved=false entries never spawn, so the shipped locker could legitimately show only the two derived traces. Keep placeholder entries limited to debug builds.

Rooms are one-way (enter_records / enter_junction), so a missed item is gone until New Game. This is accepted on purpose and softened by listing no completion counts or empty slots, but some players may still feel they missed out.
USE contention: a pickup reach that overlaps a station or hazard would take USE away from the critical path. This needs the pure overlap test and small reaches (24-28 px).

Persistence bugs: calling _save_progress() on pickup would recapture positions (lane knockdown loops) or overwrite an older save before the corridor checkpoint and disable Continue. Only the evidence part of beat_snapshot may be patched.
Existing tests compare save bytes, and m0_state_test's 'future version' fixture assumes v5 is unknown. Both need updating, and the sorted-array rule must hold or byte comparisons will flake.
Pause input routing has three entry points (PauseOverlay._input, _handle_back, _menu_focus_target). Adding a second submenu risks back or focus dead ends on controller and touch.

The audio budget and mobile cost: more generated clips, 2 step players, 2 ambience players and a reverb bus could push generation past the measured budget or strain low-end phones. Measure generation_ms and check on a device.
Decoupling sfx from the visual-effects switch changes current behaviour, and the settings copy and tests for that switch need updating.
WOLF annotations could read as chatty pet commentary and undercut his independence. Keep them sparse and authored, and include 'avert' and 'none' reactions.
Readability on phone: examine text and screen labels at a 960x540 base can be too small. The journal needs a readable default size and a scroll that works with the thumb.
Feel is unverified: none of the realism features counts as validated until the corridor, Records and Junction routes are played by hand on desktop and touch.
test_plan: item_catalog_test: ids are unique StringNames; kind is one of log/photo/data/object; chapter is in CHAPTER_IDS; essential is false for every entry; x±reach is inside the room bounds 40..920; requires names a real M0State flag; derived trace ids are flagged derived.

pickup_overlap_test (pure): for every room, no pickup reach overlaps any station or hazard USE range (corridor x<=230, 350±52, 605±52, 876±52; Records 190/520/830 ±58; Junction entry, breaker, vent grate 250-350, blast zone 360-540, door, CHOICE_X 526, bolt >=810). Lane items must have requires=sentry_down.
m0_state_test, collect(): refuses unknown, duplicate, wrong-chapter, requires-unmet and derived ids; accepts valid ones; has_item and examine/annotate keep annotated ⊆ examined ⊆ collected.

m0_state_test, derived records: the locker list contains DATA-PURGE exactly when purge_trace_preserved is true and DATA-MIRROR exactly when mirror_trace_preserved is true, and to_dict never writes them.
m0_state_test, v5 save: round-trip to_dict/from_dict gives byte-identical output with arrays written sorted; a v4 fixture loads with an empty locker; v6 is rejected as a future version.

m0_state_test, malformed v5 fixtures are each rejected: evidence not a Dictionary, non-String id, duplicate, unsorted, unknown id, approved=false id, stored derived id, examined not ⊆ collected, annotated not ⊆ examined, item chapter after chapter_id, requires flag false.

chapter_scene_test, persistence: a pickup after the corridor checkpoint, followed by a knockdown and _restore_beat, keeps the item and restores the pre-pickup checkpoint position (no lane restore point). A pickup before the safe point writes no file and leaves Continue unchanged. A pickup in Records writes only the evidence section of the save.
m0_scene_test / junction_test: a full route driven through the InputMap with zero pickups finishes every chapter, which proves nothing is gating.
spawn test: entries with approved=false create no node and no text in any room scene. A collected item shows the collected (dust outline) state after reload.

ui_controls_test: Pause has a focusable Locker button; ui_cancel from the Locker returns to Pause, then resumes; focus lands on the first row; the focus_neighbor chain wraps correctly; the touch USE label reads TAKE/READ/COPY in reach and USE otherwise; pickups are ignored while waiting_for_choice.
wall_screen_test (pure): readout(state) gives the expected lines for sampled states (purge before/after copy, gauge values, sentry idle/alert/down, breaker armed, door open).

sfx_bank_test: footstep, ambience, handling and UI clips are deterministic for SEED, peak <= PEAK, and generation stays within the existing generation_ms bound. The ambience scheduler with a fixed RNG seed produces the same event times, never repeats a chunk back to back and stops when disabled.
m0_actor footstep test: walking a known distance emits floor(distance/STRIDE_PX) stepped signals with the surface that matches the room's span data.

impact/reduce_motion test: with reduce_motion on, the pickup lean, WOLF notice tween and screen flicker leave sprite positions at their rest constants. A knockdown during a pickup lean snaps back to HUMAN_SPRITE_REST.

Not headless (reported separately, never as validated feel): rendered stills of each room with screens and props, then hands-on play of all three routes on desktop, controller and touch, then a device check of the audio budget.

options.name: Living World: grounded bodies, a breathing station and a small key kit
options.pitch: Make the slice feel physically present before it gets bigger. The engineer and WOLF gain weight: they push off and settle, step with a stride-synced gait, breathe at idle, and turn toward things that matter. Footsteps change by surface. Each room gets a quiet tone, distant hull sounds and its own reverb. Actors pick up lamp colour as they pass under fixtures, and props react to the people walking through. On top of that sits a deliberately small field kit: one find per room (a tool or a key item, Nathanial names them), plus the records the build already tracks, shown as derived entries. Every kit item is visible in the room, taken with a body action (crouch, handling sound, prop removed), reachable on foot by the engineer alone, and never required to finish. Kit items only make optional actions faster or add texture. No slots, scarcity, crafting or new on-screen buttons. The kit lives in Pause > ITEMS. Each step ships separately, is headless-tested, and is labelled unvalidated until the affected route has been played by hand.

realism_features.feature: Acceleration, deceleration and turn-around (fast in, slow out)
realism_features.player_sees: The engineer pushes off and settles a few pixels instead of sliding to a dead stop. A reverse input brakes, then turns with a short squash rather than an instant mirror. WOLF eases into position beside the engineer instead of snapping there.
realism_features.how: In M0Actor, the controlled branch becomes velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, axis*WALK_SPEED, ACCEL*delta), with ACCEL so that full speed arrives in about 0.10 s and DECEL so that a stop takes about 0.18 s. Pressing against current motion uses a TURN_DECEL about 1.6x higher. flip_h changes when the sign of velocity crosses zero, followed by a 0.08 s scale.x squash (1.0 > 0.85 > 1.0). Follow mode uses arrive steering (speed scales with distance under 48 px). The autonomous branch keeps exact arrival: once within 2 px and below 8 px/s it snaps to the target, so the ±4 px checks at RELAY_CONTACT_X and WOLF_SEAM_X still pass. Also consider WALK_SPEED 190 > ~150 (190 px/s is ~4.6 m/s, a run, at a 72 px body), but only as a separate tunable reviewed in play.

realism_features.feature: Shared stride clock and per-surface footsteps
realism_features.player_sees: Walking makes sound for the first time. The engineer's boots are heavy and dull on plate, ring on grating and slap on wet deck. WOLF's paws are lighter, quicker metal ticks with a faint servo under them. The sound changes the moment either character crosses onto a different floor.
realism_features.how: M0Actor gets stride_phase, which advances by abs(dx)/STRIDE_PX (engineer ~46 px, WOLF ~30 px) and emits stepped(foot, surface) on each wrap. Each room exports surface spans as data, e.g. PackedVector3Array(x_from, x_to, surface_index) on RoomDepth or the room script, and a static surface_at(x) looks them up. SfxBank generates 3–4 seeded variants per surface per actor: a noise transient, a band-pass body and, for grating, a ring partial. Two dedicated step AudioStreamPlayers, separate from the 4 round-robin voices, pick variants with no immediate repeat, ±6% pitch and ±2 dB jitter, so footsteps never steal a boom. Generation stays deterministic and within the measured generation_ms budget.

realism_features.feature: Pose layer: walk bob, lean, breathing idle and contact squash on the existing single sprites
realism_features.player_sees: The painted sprites stop gliding. Each stride bobs and squashes a little, the body leans into acceleration, and standing characters breathe. The engineer settles slowly and WOLF shifts with small, mechanical tilts. Floor reflections move with them.
realism_features.how: Add a pose composer to M0Actor that sets body_sprite.position/rotation/scale each frame as rest + gait (from stride_phase) + lean (from acceleration) + idle (slow sine, engineer ~3.2 s and WOLF ~2.4 s with a stepped servo ease) + reaction_offset. The existing tweens in _react_as_wolf, _fail_beat, the intro and _cancel_fail/_sync_scene are retargeted to reaction_offset/reaction_rotation instead of writing body_sprite.position directly. This removes the fight with HUMAN_SPRITE_REST/WOLF_SPRITE_REST snaps. FloorReflection already copies position/scale/rotation from the Sprite2D, so reflections follow. All amplitudes go to zero when impact.reduce_motion is on or effects are off.

realism_features.feature: Look-at and attention (authored, state-driven)
realism_features.player_sees: When the engineer stops, WOLF turns to face them or whatever is live in the room: the sentry when it is hunting, the pressure gauge while it climbs, an uncollected kit item nearby. The engineer turns toward a station while using it and glances back at WOLF during dialogue.
realism_features.how: Each room provides attention_targets(state) -> Array of {x, priority}. It is a pure function of M0State and room state (sentry_brain phase, pressure gauge, item collected), so it is deterministic and testable. M0Actor.look_at_x sets facing when the actor is idle (never mid-move against velocity) and adds a small head-first lean: rotation leads by about 0.06 s, then the body settles, following the Trico observation flagged as unverified. A 0.6 s minimum hold stops jitter between targets. WOLF's choice of target is authored. When he has just refused or disagreed, his attention rule can face away from the engineer for a beat, which shows independence through body language.

realism_features.feature: Room tone, ambient one-shots and per-room reverb
realism_features.player_sees: Rooms are never silent. The corridor has a low ventilation bed, Records a dry electrical hush, the Junction a large metal hum. Distant bangs, creaks, drips and relay clicks come at irregular moments from left or right. Impacts and footsteps tail off differently in each room: tight and metallic in the corridor, deadened in Records, long in the Junction.
realism_features.how: A new code-created 'Room' bus (send to Master) holds an AudioEffectReverb whose room_size/damping/wet/predelay/hipass are set from a per-room preset on room entry. Footsteps and SfxBank voices route through it; UI does not. Room tone comes from 3–4 seeded procedural chunks per room (filtered noise plus low partials), crossfaded in a random order so the loop is not noticeable. A seeded scheduler fires 6–8 procedural one-shots at random times (4–14 s apart) with random pan via AudioStreamPlayer2D x, pitch and volume. One-shots respond to state where it makes sense, e.g. the Junction's creaks thin out after the door blast and relay clicks stop once the corridor relay is set. This also fixes the existing coupling: sfx_bank.enabled stops following the visual effects toggle, and audio is controlled only by the bus sliders.

realism_features.feature: Lamp tint and pools of light on actors (no Light2D)
realism_features.player_sees: Walking under a fixture brightens the engineer and WOLF and tints them in that lamp's colour. Between lamps they fall back into shadow. Warning lamps wash them red while a klaxon state is active. The reflections pick up the same tint.
realism_features.how: RoomDepth exposes lamp_world_x() (converting the lamps plate fractions through the 0.9 parallax) and a static light_at(x, state) that sums Gaussian falloffs of lamp_color plus warning_color when active, mixed over a per-room ambient base. M0Actor lerps body_sprite.modulate toward it at about 6/s, and FloorReflection already copies modulate. This avoids the Light2D/normal-map cost and works the same on GL Compatibility mobile. Lamp flicker tweens can drive the same value so actors flicker with their lamp.

realism_features.feature: Reactive props and contact particles
realism_features.player_sees: Small puffs of grit lift from grating under each footfall. Hanging cables and tags swing when someone brushes past and settle again. Puddles on wet spans ripple. A dropped tank and the door blast leave lasting debris. Kit items glint until they are taken and are gone afterwards.
realism_features.how: Each stepped signal feeds a pooled one-shot CPUParticles2D (4–6 particles, surface-coloured; off when reduce_motion is on or effects are off). A code-drawn Swing Node2D (a damped spring on rotation) is kicked by actor velocity when an actor's x crosses its span. A Ripple Node2D draws expanding ellipses on stepped events in wet spans. Debris states are driven by existing flags (door_blown, tank dropped), so they survive restore without new save fields. Prop placement is data per room and avoids every station and hazard reach range.

realism_features.feature: Optional art upgrade: stride-synced walk frames (gated on Nathanial's approval)
realism_features.player_sees: Real leg motion: an 8-frame walk for the engineer and a 6–8 frame trot for WOLF, timed to the same stride clock, so feet stop skating and the footsteps land with them.
realism_features.how: Generate side-view walk strips in the named WOLF//OVERRIDE ChatGPT/Codex image_gen project to the approved outfit (deep-red hooded field jacket, charcoal trousers and boots, minimal cyan light; WOLF's existing body). Clean the frames into one sheet per character, re-imported at on-screen scale (fixing today's ~8–10 MB VRAM per sprite), and use Sprite2D hframes with frame = floor(stride_phase * N). The single painted sprite stays as the idle and fallback frame. The pose layer still adds lean and breathing on top. A cutout rig (Polygon2D + Skeleton2D) is not recommended for this slice: it needs split painted parts and weight painting, and the painterly sprites would show seams. Only start this if a played build shows procedural bob is not enough.

inventory.what_you_collect: A small field kit. Each room has one physical find (a tool or a key item), and the case also shows read-only record entries derived from flags the save already holds (the purge trace and mirror trace). Finds are painted or code-drawn props in the room with an available glint. They are taken with a crouch or lean, a handling sound, and the prop leaving the scene. There is no slot limit, no consumables, no crafting and no combining. At most three kit items exist in this slice.
item_kinds: Tool: permanent, stays visible on the engineer as a small code-drawn detail, and never spent
Key item: used automatically at the one station it belongs to, then marked spent and kept in the list as used
Record (derived): read-only entries computed from existing state flags such as purge_trace_preserved and mirror_trace_preserved; never stored twice
example_items_per_room: Maintenance corridor: [TOOL A], e.g. a clip-on work light, at roughly x 680 in the free span before the seal (reach 26 px; clear of the breaker, relay and purge display). Once carried it shows as a small cyan clip on the engineer and lifts their lamp-tint floor in dark spans, so it changes feel only. It is never needed to see anything.

Records Access: [KEY ITEM B] at roughly x 340 in the hazard-free 248–462 span (the best first pickup to build). At one copy station it adds an optional authored inspection beat or shortens that station's hold slightly. Copying works the same without it.

Service Junction: [KEY ITEM C], e.g. a bolt driver or crank handle, at roughly x 100 in the safe entry span (40–148; never at the vent grate, blast zone, door or the live lane). At the exit bolt it is used automatically and shortens the hand crank (e.g. hold ~1.6 s > ~1.0 s). The bare-hand crank stays fully valid.
Derived records (all rooms): entries for the purge trace and mirror trace, listed from the existing flags using lines already in the build. Nathanial writes any new record text.
inventory.how_items_are_used: Contextually with the existing USE, never by selecting an item. In reach of a find, the hint reads 'E: take [NAME]' and the touch USE label shows TAKE. At the matching station the hint changes to name the item (e.g. 'Hold E: crank with [NAME]'), and USE uses it automatically, marking it spent. A tool is passive while carried. Pickups are checked at the top of _interact() after the save_pending retry, with a reach of 24–28 px that a pure test proves never overlaps a station or hazard range. The pickup plays a 0.25 s crouch through the pose layer's reaction_offset, a procedural handling sound (cloth rustle plus small metal tick) and a short non-interactive pickup card in the HUD (2 s, static when reduce_motion is on).
inventory.ui: Pause gets an ITEMS button (reflow: Resume, Items, Settings, Return to Title, 52 px buttons, panel ~450 tall). It opens an InventoryMenu sibling of SettingsMenu in the expanded 760×464 layout, using the game presentation, not the terminal theme. The left column is KIT: up to 3 rows, each with a code-drawn icon, name and a CARRIED/USED text label (never colour alone). The right column is RECORDS (derived). Selecting a row shows examine text and, if earned, WOLF's annotation in a lower pane. Rows are at least 64 px tall for touch and use explicit focus_neighbor paths with grab_focus on open. Back/cancel go through PauseOverlay._input, main._handle_back() and _menu_focus_target() the same way Settings does. Long text uses the escaped RichTextLabel scrolling already used for Credits and the changelog. No new on-screen HUD button.
inventory.wolf_role: WOLF notices and does not fetch. When the engineer comes within ~90 px of an uncollected find, the find becomes WOLF's top attention target: he turns to it, leans in head-first and gives one soft servo chirp, once per item per visit. This is authored and gated by memory. Right after he has refused or disagreed in that room he may withhold the cue, which shows his independence without blocking anything. In the case, an item WOLF reacted to can carry a short WOLF annotation that Nathanial writes and approves; it is unlocked by real observed state, such as the item being used. WOLF never carries, uses or gates an item, so he does not become a pack mule or a spectator-making helper.
inventory.engineer_fallback: Every find sits on open, hazard-free floor that the engineer reaches by walking, and is marked by its own glint and the USE hint, with no WOLF cue needed. No kit item is required. Each one only makes an optional action faster or adds texture, so the corridor relay manual reroute, Records copying and the Junction bolt all work exactly as they do now without any item. Rooms are one-way, so a missed find is simply missed. Nothing on the critical path checks inventory, and a test proves it.
inventory.save_model: SAVE_VERSION 5. to_dict adds "inventory": {"collected": [...], "spent": [...]} with ids written sorted so save bytes stay deterministic. Item definitions live in a code-defined ItemCatalog (RefCounted constants: id, kind, chapter, x, reach, requires, essential=false, approved). Player-facing text lives in a separate Nathanial-owned text file, and approved=false items never spawn. from_dict adds a fourth 'if version >= 5' block after the v4 block: inventory must be a Dictionary with Array-of-String lists, no duplicates, every id in the catalog, spent ⊆ collected, each item's chapter at or before the saved chapter_id, each requires flag true, and a spent item's station flag consistent. Saves below v5 load with an empty kit and nothing is granted retroactively; derived records come from existing flags automatically. A pickup changes state and patches only the inventory field of beat_snapshot (keeping its positions), then calls _write_beat() only if checkpoint_reached. It never calls _save_progress(), so a pickup cannot move the restore point into a hazard lane or overwrite a save before the safe point. Knockdown/restore keeps whatever was collected before the snapshot.

options.input_mapping: No new actions and no new on-screen buttons. Keyboard: hold move_left/move_right (A/D or arrows by default) to walk with the new acceleration; interact (E by default) is pressed to take a find in reach and held at a station, which uses a matching key item automatically; choice_1/choice_2 are unchanged; pause_game opens Pause, where ITEMS is navigated with arrow keys plus Enter and closed with Esc/back. Controller: stick/D-pad to move, the interact button (A by default) to take or use, START to pause, and D-pad/stick with A/B inside the ITEMS menu through explicit focus neighbours. Touch: the existing hold-to-move pads; the existing USE button relabels to TAKE when a find is in reach; the existing top-right Pause opens the menu, where rows are tapped (64 px or more) and the list drag-scrolls, ignoring emulated mouse events like the changelog does. All bindings stay remappable through the existing GameSettings rebind flow, and every hint reads the live binding label.
options.art_needed: Base plan, all code-drawn so no new art provenance is needed: three kit-prop Node2Ds with an available glint (through RoomDepth.make_glow), three matching 32–40 px inventory icons, the work-light clip detail on the engineer, Swing cables/tags, Ripple puddles, debris marks and step-dust particles. Optional upgrade: 8-frame engineer walk and 6–8 frame WOLF trot strips generated in the named WOLF//OVERRIDE ChatGPT/Codex image_gen project, matched to the approved outfit and WOLF's existing design, cleaned into sheets, and logged in apps/game/assets/manifest.json with source conversation, date and provisional rights. Nathanial approves the art before it is merged. Painted kit-prop variants for each room can also come later through the same route. Manifest entries must wait until the in-progress manifest.json merge conflict is resolved.
options.audio_needed: All procedural in SfxBank with the existing seed, so the provenance is 'code-generated in this repository': footsteps per surface (plate, grate, wet) per actor (boot, paw) with 3–4 variants each; a WOLF servo sweetener under steps; 3–4 room-tone chunks for each of the three rooms; 6–8 ambient one-shots (distant hull bang, creak, drip, relay click, vent flutter, far klaxon tail); and pickup and use handling sounds (cloth rustle, small metal tick, tool seat clunk). Room reverb uses built-in AudioEffectReverb presets on a code-created Room bus. If procedural steps prove too thin in play, CC0 footstep packs (e.g. Kenney) are the fallback, logged in the manifest with licence and URL. No music or voice is added.
risks: Feel claims cannot be validated headlessly. Every step stays labelled 'implemented, not played' until Nathanial or an agent plays the affected route in one normal Godot window with a separate test save, as AGENT.md and PRIVATE_AGENTS.md require.

Acceleration and arrive steering can break the existing exact-position logic (±4 px at RELAY_CONTACT_X and WOLF_SEAM_X, the sentry lane timing, the knockdown margins) and the scene tests that walk via InputMap. Keep the autonomous branch exact-landing, and expect to update the test margins.

The pose-layer refactor touches every tween that writes body_sprite.position directly (_react_as_wolf, _fail_beat, the intro, _cancel_fail, _sync_scene). A missed site gives double offsets or a sprite stuck off rest after restore.

Procedural footsteps and room tone can sound synthetic or fatiguing. The per-room bed plus one-shots needs a level and mix pass on device speakers. Generation time must stay inside the generation_ms bound (about 40 ms today), so precompute only what each room needs, on entry.

Mobile cost: more AudioStreamPlayers, a reverb on a bus and particle pools on low-end GL Compatibility devices. Particles and reverb need off switches tied to the existing effects/reduce_motion settings, and the frame budget is untested on devices.
Decoupling sfx_bank.enabled from the visual-effects toggle changes current behaviour, so the settings docs and tests must be updated in the same step.

Inventory scope creep: pressure to add slots, consumables or weapons. The private direction keeps the pair non-lethal toward people and has no morality meter, so items must stay keys, tools and records only.
Item names, examine text and WOLF annotations are story text. Nothing ships until Nathanial approves it (approved=false never spawns), so the system can be ready while showing nothing.
Optional walk-frame art may not stay consistent with the painted idle sprites or the approved outfit, and it needs his approval. That is why it is the last, gated step.

The worktree is mid-merge (manifest.json has conflict markers). Provenance entries and any 'merge everything into main' work have to wait until that conflict is resolved, and the Notion board must be updated afterwards through Codex, as the user asked; there is no automatic sync.
test_plan: m0_actor accel test: from rest with axis=1 the controlled actor reaches WALK_SPEED within the target time ±1 frame; after release it stops within the target distance; a reverse input decelerates harder than a release.
Autonomous arrival test: WOLF given autonomous_target_x lands within ±0.5 px and at zero velocity in bounded frames, so the existing RELAY_CONTACT_X and WOLF_SEAM_X checks still pass.
Stride clock test: walking a known distance emits floor(distance/STRIDE_PX) stepped signals for each actor; standing still emits none; feet alternate.
Surface lookup test: surface_at(x) returns the right surface for each room's span table; spans cover 40..920 with no gaps or overlaps.

SfxBank footstep/ambience test: buffers are byte-identical across two generate() runs with the fixed seed, peak level stays at or below PEAK, every surface/actor/variant exists, total generation stays under the existing bound, and steps never take one of the 4 round-robin voices.
Room bus test: entering each room sets the expected reverb parameters on the Room bus; sfx_bank stays enabled when the visual-effects toggle is off.
Pose layer test: with reduce_motion on, gait/lean/idle offsets are exactly zero; after _sync_scene/_cancel_fail the sprite composes to exactly HUMAN_SPRITE_REST/WOLF_SPRITE_REST.
Attention target test: for fixed M0State fixtures (sentry hunting, gauge rising, item uncollected or collected, recent refusal) attention_targets() returns the expected ordered targets.
Lamp tint test: light_at(x) peaks at each lamp's world x and falls off symmetrically; warning tint is added only when its state flag is set.
Catalog/layout test: every item's reach range in every room is inside the documented free spans and never overlaps a station, hazard, blast, vent, lane, bolt or CHOICE_X range.
Collect test: collect() rejects unknown ids, duplicates, the wrong chapter and unmet requires; the matching station marks the item spent; collected and spent stay sorted.
Critical-path test: both complete routes (WOLF-help and engineer-only) finish all three rooms with an empty kit, and also with every item collected.

Save v5 tests: round-trip byte equality; a v4 fixture loads with an empty kit and unchanged progress; malformed fixtures fail validation (non-dict inventory, non-string id, duplicate, unknown id, spent not in collected, future-chapter item, unmet requires); the 'unknown future version' fixture moves to 6.

Pickup persistence test: a pickup before the corridor safe point writes nothing to disk and keeps Continue's state; after the checkpoint it writes only an inventory change, so the restored positions equal the prior snapshot; a knockdown after the pickup keeps the item.

Pause ITEMS UI test: open from Pause, initial focus is grabbed, focus neighbours cycle through all rows and back, back/cancel returns to Pause through _handle_back, row heights are at least 64 px, status uses text labels and not just colour, and an unapproved item never appears.

scores.name: FIELD KIT: carried tools and key items that change how stations are solved
scores.note: This draft has the strongest inventory design. Items are physical props in the room, tools stay visible on the engineer, and key items are fitted automatically at their station. It does little for the slice's biggest realism gaps, though: there is still no footstep or room sound, and movement still starts and stops instantly. Three choices raise the risk. Dropping the valve to 2 turns (TURNS_NEEDED is 3 today) shortens the vent and blast window and retunes a puzzle no one has played. The scarce pin stays spent after a knockdown. WOLF detours to scan or fetch items, which brushes against the ±4 px event positions. Fetching also starts to make WOLF a pack mule. Trim WOLF to noticing items only, and leave the scarce pin until after a played build.

scores.name: Evidence Locker
scores.note: This fits the game's tone and abstract direction best: corroborating records, nothing ever spent, no completion counts, and WOLF as a witness. Room tone, per-room reverb, footsteps and wall screens that read real state target the gaps the research ranks highest. The inventory's value depends heavily on story text. Until Nathanial approves entries, the locker can honestly show only the two traces derived from existing flags. Read-only items also change nothing in play. The wall-screen readout(state) function is cheap and very testable. Its stated risk that manifest.json is mid-merge is stale: the worktree is clean, it merged main at 934f1b2, and manifest.json parses.

scores.name: Living World: grounded bodies, a breathing station and a small key kit
scores.note: This draft answers 'feel more REAL' most directly. It adds acceleration and deceleration, a stride clock with per-surface footsteps, a pose layer (bob, lean, breathing), state-driven look-at, and room tone with reverb. The pose-layer refactor is the right structural fix: about 13 places in main.gd write body_sprite position or REST directly, so they would be retargeted to a reaction offset. It is also the riskiest single change, along with acceleration near the exact-landing checks. The three-item kit is thin. One example is wrong: the exit bolt is a 0.6 s whine charge (BOLT_WHINE_SECONDS) at BOLT_X, not a 1.6 s hold. The walk-frame art (3 days) and lamp tint should be later steps that need approval.

final_options.name: A. Grounded Bodies and Breathing Rooms (realism first, no inventory)
final_options.pitch: This option makes the existing three rooms feel physically present before adding anything new to collect. The engineer and WOLF gain weight and sound, and every room gets a voice. It changes no puzzle, no story text and no save format, so it can ship in small steps that each stay off by default until played. It answers the 'feel more REAL' half of the request on its own and gives Options B and C the stride clock, handling sounds and Room bus they depend on.

realism_features.feature: Per-surface footsteps from a shared stride clock
realism_features.player_sees: Walking makes sound for the first time. The engineer's boots fall heavy and the change from plate to grating to wet deck is audible. WOLF's paws are lighter, quicker metal ticks with a faint servo under them. The Junction vent grate sounds hollow.
realism_features.how: M0Actor gets stride_phase, which advances by abs(dx)/STRIDE_PX (about 46 px for the engineer and 30 px for WOLF) and emits stepped(foot, surface) each time it wraps. Each room supplies surface spans as data, and a static surface_at(x) looks them up. SfxBank generates 3–4 seeded variants per surface per actor and plays them on 2 dedicated step players, so steps never take one of the 4 round-robin voices. Each step gets a no-repeat variant pick, ±6% pitch and ±2 dB volume.

realism_features.feature: Room tone, ambient one-shots and per-room reverb
realism_features.player_sees: No room is ever silent. The corridor hums with ventilation, Records has a dry electrical hush and the Junction has a big metal drone. Distant bangs, ticks, drips and relay clicks arrive at irregular times. Footsteps and impacts tail off tight in the corridor, deadened in Records and long in the Junction. Some ambient sounds follow real state; for example, Junction creaks thin out after the door blast.
realism_features.how: Add a code-created Room bus with an AudioEffectReverb, set from a per-room preset on enter_records and enter_junction. Room tone is 3–4 seeded procedural chunks per room played in a no-repeat order. A seeded Timer schedules one-shots on AudioStreamPlayer2D nodes at the room edges. sfx_bank.enabled also stops following the visual-effects toggle (main._apply_effects line 328). That changes how an existing setting behaves, so Nathanial confirms it first.

realism_features.feature: Acceleration, deceleration and turn-around (fast in, slow out)
realism_features.player_sees: The engineer pushes off and settles instead of starting and stopping dead. Reversing brakes first, then turns with a short squash. WOLF eases into position beside the engineer instead of snapping there.
realism_features.how: In the controlled branch, use velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, axis*WALK_SPEED, ACCEL*delta), reaching full speed in about 0.10 s, stopping in about 0.18 s, with harder braking on a reverse input. Follow mode uses arrive steering inside 48 px. The autonomous branch keeps exact landing: within 2 px and below 8 px/s it snaps to the target, so the RELAY_CONTACT_X and WOLF_SEAM_X checks still pass. Treat WALK_SPEED 190 as its own tunable and change it only after play.

realism_features.feature: Pose layer: walk bob, lean and breathing idle on the existing single sprites
realism_features.player_sees: The painted sprites stop gliding. Each stride bobs slightly, the body leans into acceleration and settles out of it, and standing characters breathe: the engineer slowly, WOLF with small stepped mechanical tilts. Floor reflections follow automatically.
realism_features.how: A composer in M0Actor sets body_sprite position, rotation and scale each frame as rest + gait + lean + idle + reaction_offset. The about 13 direct writes in main.gd (_react_as_wolf, _fail_beat, the intro, _cancel_fail, _sync_scene) move to reaction_offset. Every amplitude is zero when reduce_motion is on or effects are off.

realism_features.feature: State-driven attention (look-at)
realism_features.player_sees: When the engineer stops, WOLF faces whatever is live in the room: the sentry while it hunts, the gauge while it climbs, the engineer otherwise. Right after he refuses or disagrees, he may hold a look away for a beat. The engineer turns toward a station while using it.
realism_features.how: Each room provides a pure attention_targets(state) function that returns prioritised x positions. Facing changes only when the actor is idle, with a 0.6 s minimum hold to stop jitter. A refusal look-away is an authored rule, not a meter.

inventory.what_you_collect: Nothing new in this option. It deliberately contains no inventory and covers only the realism half of the request. Kit-relevant pieces are built here and reused by B and C: the stride clock, the handling-sound generator and the Room bus.
item_kinds: None in this option (see B and C)
example_items_per_room: Corridor: no items; surface spans of plate and grating, a ventilation bed
Records Access: no items; a damped reverb preset and an electrical hush
Service Junction: no items; a wet-deck span, a hollow vent grate, a long reverb, and creaks tied to door_blown
inventory.ui: No new UI. One settings change: the visual-effects toggle no longer mutes sound, and the settings copy for that toggle is updated to match.
inventory.wolf_role: Only his body language changes: paw steps, servo, look-at, and a refusal look-away driven by existing memory state. His choices and events are unchanged.
inventory.engineer_fallback: No objective changes, so every existing engineer-only path is untouched. The acceleration step must keep exact autonomous landing, and the scene tests that walk via InputMap must still complete both routes.
inventory.save_model: No save change: SAVE_VERSION stays 4. Debris and room-tone states come from existing flags such as door_blown and the tank drop, so they survive a restore without new fields.

final_options.input_mapping: No changes. move_left/move_right, interact, choice_1/choice_2 and pause_game behave as before, and remapping is unaffected. The only thing a player feels is acceleration, and input response stays immediate (no anticipation delay).
final_options.art_needed: None required. Optional step-dust particles (CPUParticles2D) are code-only. Walk-cycle frames are a separate later decision: Codex image_gen strips that need Nathanial's approval and manifest entries. They are not part of this option.
final_options.audio_needed: All procedural and seeded in SfxBank: footsteps (3 surfaces, 2 actors, 3–4 variants each), a WOLF servo layer under his steps, 3–4 room-tone chunks per room, and 6–8 ambient one-shots. Reverb uses the built-in AudioEffectReverb. Generation stays inside the existing sfx_bank_test bound (under 400 ms), with per-room clips generated on room entry if needed. CC0 footsteps (for example Kenney) are a fallback only if procedural steps sound thin in play, and would be logged in the manifest.
risks: Acceleration or arrive steering could break the exact ±4 px event checks and the margins in the InputMap-driven scene tests.
The pose-layer refactor touches every tween that writes body_sprite directly. Missing one leaves a double offset or a sprite stuck off its rest pose after a restore.
Procedural steps and room tone can sound synthetic or tiring. They need a mix pass on device speakers.
More audio players, a reverb bus and particles add cost on low-end GL Compatibility phones, and that cost has not been measured.
Decoupling sound from the visual-effects toggle changes current behaviour and needs Nathanial's sign-off.
No feel claim is valid until the corridor, Records and Junction routes are played by hand.
test_plan: Stride clock: walking a known distance emits floor(distance/STRIDE_PX) steps per actor; standing still emits none; feet alternate.
surface_at(x) returns the right surface for each room's spans, and the spans cover 40..920 with no gaps or overlaps.
sfx_bank_test: new clips are byte-deterministic for SEED, peak at or below PEAK, stay within the generation bound, and step players never take a round-robin voice.
Room bus: each room entry sets the expected reverb parameters, and sfx stays enabled when visual effects are off.
Ambience scheduler: a fixed seed gives the same event times, no chunk repeats back to back, and it stops when disabled.
Acceleration: reaches WALK_SPEED in the target time ±1 frame, stops within the target distance, and brakes harder on reverse. Autonomous WOLF lands within 0.5 px at zero velocity.
Pose layer: every offset is exactly zero with reduce_motion on, and after _sync_scene or _cancel_fail the sprite is exactly at HUMAN_SPRITE_REST / WOLF_SPRITE_REST.
attention_targets() returns the expected ordered targets for fixed M0State fixtures.
Both full routes (WOLF-help and engineer-only) still complete headless.
Label the evidence: the items above are headless logic only. Rendered stills and hands-on play of each route are reported separately.

final_options.name: B. Evidence Case (records-first inventory with physical pickups)
final_options.pitch: The engineer carries a case of evidence. It holds copied logs, data fragments, prints and a few physical objects, each picked up from the room with a body action and a handling sound. The two records the critical path already produces (the purge trace and the mirror trace) appear automatically, derived from existing flags, so the case is useful on day one even before any new story text is approved. Nothing in it is ever spent, gates progress, has a slot or counts toward completion. Wall screens that show live system state give the rooms a working, diegetic life, and optional logs are copied from them with the existing hold-to-use. WOLF is a witness who reacts to some finds and may annotate them; he never carries anything.

realism_features.feature: Items exist physically, and their absence leaves a mark
realism_features.player_sees: A small prop sits among the room's dressing with a faint glint, brighter when the engineer is in reach. Once taken it is gone, and a clean dust outline shows where it lay. The room looks the same after a reload.
realism_features.how: A code-drawn Node2D per pickup, in the ValveWheel/TankArt style, with three states: available, in_reach and taken. The state comes from state.has_item(id) and the engineer's x position. The glint uses RoomDepth.make_glow. Reach is 24–28 px, placed only on free-floor spans.

realism_features.feature: Pickup as a body action (follow-through, no input delay)
realism_features.player_sees: The engineer dips and leans toward the item for about 0.25 s. The item lifts and fades toward them with a sound that matches its material (paper rustle, plastic clack, tag clink, data chirp). A short 'Logged: [NAME]' line appears in the objective panel. With Reduce Motion on, only the fade and the sound play.
realism_features.how: A tween on reaction_offset (Option A's pose layer), or on body_sprite through the existing snap-back to REST if A has not shipped yet. Handling sounds come from seeded SfxBank clips on one dedicated player. Controls stay live throughout.

realism_features.feature: Wall screens driven by real state
realism_features.player_sees: Small CRT panels show what the systems are actually doing: purge queue progress in Records, line pressure and door-lock state at the valve, sentry status in the lane, breaker and relay readouts in the corridor. They change the moment the state changes. Holding USE copies an optional log, with a progress bar from 0 to 100%.
realism_features.how: A code-drawn WallScreen (ColorRect bezel, Label, scanlines drawn in _draw with no shader). A pure static readout(state) returns PackedStringArray, so tests can check it without a scene. Copying reuses hold_use.gd. Flicker honours reduce_motion. Nathanial approves all readout wording.

realism_features.feature: WOLF notices on his own terms
realism_features.player_sees: When the engineer lingers in reach of certain finds with WOLF close by, WOLF turns toward the item with a head dip and an ear-servo whine, or pointedly looks away, or does nothing. An annotation may appear in the case later.
realism_features.how: Each catalog entry has an authored wolf_reaction: notice, avert or none. It triggers only after the engineer has been in reach for more than 1 s and WOLF is within about 120 px, so he never acts as a metal detector. He does not move from his follow position, so no event position is ever disturbed.

inventory.what_you_collect: Optional evidence (logs copied from screens, data fragments, prints, small objects with examine text), plus the derived trace records. No consumables, slots, scarcity or completion counts.
item_kinds: RECORD (derived): the purge trace and mirror trace, listed from purge_trace_preserved and mirror_trace_preserved and never stored
LOG: copied from a wall screen by holding USE
DATA / PRINT: a fragment or image picked up with a tap
OBJECT: a physical artefact with examine text, possibly with a WOLF annotation later
example_items_per_room: Corridor: [LOG_CORRIDOR] on a screen in the free span between the breaker and the relay (about x 440–520); [OBJECT_CORRIDOR] before the seal (about x 690–740)

final_options.name: C. Field Kit (a few tools and key items you carry and fit)
final_options.pitch: The engineer picks up a small field kit of at most 4 physical entries across the three rooms, plus the derived records. A tool stays with the engineer, visible on the hip, and gives one existing station an optional, physically shown alternative. Seated in the valve, it ratchets with each hold tick. A key item is fitted automatically at the one station it belongs to and then marked spent; that station keeps its current engineer-only method. This option is the one where what you collect changes how you play, but every change is optional, and both the empty-kit and full-kit routes are tested. Scarcity (the spare release pin) and WOLF fetching are held back until a played build shows they are wanted.

judged.recommendation: Build A first, then the B case, then one C tool, behind the shared foundation. Option A is the most direct answer to 'feel more REAL'. It needs no story text and no save change. Footsteps, room tone and reverb fill the build's most obvious gap, which is silence while moving. Acceleration and the pose layer remove the gliding sprites. A also produces the stride clock, handling sounds and Room bus the other options reuse. Next, deliver the inventory as B's evidence case, because it matches the game's tone and abstract direction best and is useful at once: the derived purge and mirror records fill it without any new text. Its first physical pickup goes in Records Access, the room with no hazards. Once that pickup has been played, add exactly one C tool, carried on the hip and ratcheting in the valve, so collecting can also change play. Keep the turn count at 3 until the junction has been played. Defer the scarce spare pin, any WOLF fetching or detours, lamp tint and walk-cycle art until a played build asks for them. Two corrections to the drafts: the worktree's mid-merge state is resolved (branch codex/game-presentation is clean, merged main at 934f1b2, and manifest.json parses), and the exit bolt is a 0.6 s whine, not a 1.6 s hold. No feel claim is valid until each affected route has been played by hand.

build_order: 1. Stride clock and per-surface footsteps (engineer and WOLF) on dedicated step players. Headless tests, then play the corridor by hand.
2. Decouple sound from the visual-effects toggle (after Nathanial approves) and add the Room bus with per-room reverb. Update the settings copy and tests in the same step.

3. Room tone chunks and the seeded ambient one-shot scheduler, room by room (corridor, Records, Junction), with state-tied sounds such as creaks thinning after door_blown. Check the generation budget, then play each room.
4. Acceleration, deceleration and arrive steering with exact autonomous landing. Rerun the RELAY_CONTACT_X and WOLF_SEAM_X tests and play both routes.
5. Pose-layer refactor (move the direct body_sprite writes to reaction_offset), then add gait bob, lean and breathing idle. Rendered stills, then play.

6. M0State v5 save (fields, validation, migration, sorted bytes) and ItemCatalog, with derived records only. The Pause CASE/KIT screen ships showing just the purge and mirror traces. No story text is needed for this step.
7. The first physical pickup in Records Access (hazard-free): prop states, overlap test, crouch through reaction_offset, handling sound, toast, snapshot-only persistence. Play Records by hand.
8. Wall screens with a pure readout(state), first in Records, then the junction valve and lane. Optional log copying uses hold_use. Readout wording waits for Nathanial.
9. Remaining approved finds in the corridor and the Junction entry, plus WOLF notice/avert reactions (no detours).
10. One field-kit tool: the hip silhouette (approved from a still), the valve ratchet at the same 3 turns, and the carry rattle. Play the junction, then decide whether to retune.

11. Deferred, only if wanted after play: State-driven attention/look-at, lamp tint, the spare-pin scarce choice, WOLF fetching one optional find, and Codex image_gen walk-cycle strips with manifest entries.
questions_for_user: Is the inventory mainly evidence (records and finds you read, nothing spent), mainly a kit (tools and key items that change how a station is solved), or a mix, as recommended: evidence first plus one tool? And should anything ever be scarce, such as a single spare-pin decision, or stay non-scarce in this slice?

What should the case or kit be called in the Pause menu, and will you write the names, examine text and any WOLF annotations for the first 3–5 items, starting with the one Records Access pickup? Until you do, nothing beyond the two derived trace records will spawn.
May turning off the visual-effects toggle stop muting all sound? Today it silences SfxBank too, which would also silence footsteps, room tone and pickup sounds.
How should WOLF relate to items: only notice or pointedly ignore them (recommended), or also scan and mark them, or fetch one optional find under his existing memory rule?

Should collected items, and a spent key item, survive a knockdown restore as designed (the pickup is patched into the snapshot)? And may a tool ever make a station faster, such as fewer valve turns, or only change how the action looks and sounds until you have played it?
